text:
evan: Heads up—noticed a reproducible repetition loop on Confluence13B after int4 quant. Happens on long contexts (>2k). Looks like tokens keep echoing a 32-token window.

maria: repro steps? model variant, tokenizer, seq len, and batch size?

evan: confluence13b_bf16 -> confluence13b_int4 (ours). Tokenizer: confluence-v1 (based on gemma spm). Seq=4096, batch=1, sampling temp=0.7.

jong: Saw similar with a different model last month where rotary freq scaling + sparse attention mask interacted badly after quant. Any logs?

maria: ran quick eval, got this on longstory benchmark: 9/10 runs show early repetition at ~2100 tokens. Perplexity spikes.

sophie: can you dump kv cache head stats? might be headwise phase wrap.

ci-bot: autotest run started: run_eval.sh --model confluence13b_int4 --task longstory --seq 4096 --seed 42

ci-bot: result (quick): repetition onset 2104 tokens, top tokens locked to "the" "and" pattern.

evan: logging shows rotary angles go near pi boundary, then several heads collapse. suspect our rotary scale mismatch when converting from gemma-style freqs to mixed head dims.

jong: Confluence was hybrid: some layers use gemma-style per-head freqs, others use llm-style scaled freqs. If quantized weights compress scale factors, rotary phase accumulation could alias. Try forcing per-layer freq normalization to float32 during inference.

maria: patch test: set rotary_scale_override = 1.0 for layers 10-16 and run int4. Command: 
```
python infra/run_infer.py --model confluence13b_int4 --override rotary_scale:10-16:1.0 --seq 4096
```
ci-bot: patched run queued.

ci-bot: patched run done: repetition still appears but onset pushed to 2350 tokens, less severe.

sophie: that suggests quant noise on scale factors is amplifying wrap. Another angle: tokenizer may map some control chars to same id (zero-width or soft hyphen) causing local token repetition amplification. Can you grep for repeated token ids at onset?

maria: dump of token ids around onset (2100..2110):
```
[1402, 330, 12, 987, 330, 12, 987, 330, 12, 987]
```
That's suspicious: repeating pattern of three ids.

evan: that points to tokenizer aliasing. Confluence-v1 spm merge created surrogate tokens for zero-width joiner sequences. In int4 build we use a remapped vocab table (to reduce ids) and might have created an alias inadvertently.

jong: two things to try in parallel: 1) run int4 with rotary_scale as fp32 and kv cache accumulation in fp32 (to test numeric path), 2) run int4 but with tokenizer remap disabled (use raw ids).

anna: spinning up both runs now. Run A: rotary+kv fp32. Run B: tokenizer raw ids.

ci-bot: Run A complete — repetition eliminated in 10/10 quick runs. Perf cost +6% latency.

ci-bot: Run B complete — repetition reduced but not eliminated. Token id stream no longer shows exact 3-id loop but still some echo.

sophie: conclusion: primary culprit is numeric drift in rotary accumulation under int4; tokenizer aliasing compounds the effect. Remediation: keep rotary scale and kv accumulation in fp32 for now, and fix vocab remap to preserve uniqueness for zero-width sequences.

maria: opened PR #4281 to change quant pipeline for rotary constants and to add a regression test (longstory seq=4096). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/confluence/pull/4281

evan: nice. also add an eval in nightly that checks for repeating-id loops (pattern detection) so this doesn't regress.

jong: note for release notes: confluence13b_int4 known limitation: we keep rotary constants in fp32 to avoid rare long-context repetition; perf tradeoff documented.

sophie: will follow up on tokenizer remap edge-case and propose a safe id remapping that preserves zero-width uniqueness.

evan: thanks all. assigning follow-ups: maria -> tests/PR, jong -> perf impact analysis, sophie -> tokenizer remap patch. cc @product for release note draft. :thumbsup:
